build: Build 04 before any changes after this review

ratings.reason: Clear improvements in wayfinding, functional text, recovery feedback, memory identity, and extraction staging. Art fidelity, authored performance/animation, encounter variety and narrative payoff remain well below AAA production readiness. These are limited agent judgments, not human-study scores or a perfection certification.

methods: Installed Chrome headless via Playwright at1440x900; inspected actual menu, graphics settings, spawn, nearby site, recovery progress, memory, extraction and result screenshots.
Normal controls with active enemies on Recon: W2s, A4.7s, W6.1s. The straight-line route met cover at x-24.29,z1.16,16.16m from West Archive; this was not a full blind objective completion.

Explicit debug teleport then positioned the player2m from West core for real hold-E interaction. Remaining cores were debug-collected and player moved to insertion to inspect active extraction; four-second hold completed with19 enemies active.
Read UI source to identify remaining small label sizes and message-routing/pause-memory behavior. No source files edited.
improvementsObserved: At spawn all three named core markers and distances are immediately visible, reducing dependence on tiny radar.
Hold-E progress is visible; recovered core becomes a named person with a readable quote; corresponding pylon dims green and crystal disappears.
Functional health/ammunition/objective text is larger. Graphics selector is visible and dialog fits1440x900.
Extraction has a green beacon, explicit progress panel, hold instruction and a finite four-second stage rather than instant completion.
Directional damage cue appeared during extraction and victory panel rendered correctly.

findings.problem: A recovered memory is only visible in a7.5s transient card during active combat. Pause hides HUD while the timeout continues. A player cannot safely pause to read the new story payload.
findings.evidence: Actual memory card screenshot plus main.js event timeout and pause HUD visibility.
findings.recommendation: Persist recovered quotes in a pause/archive log; make them readable after the card disappears.

findings.problem: Current event handler routes all nonempty kill/supply messages to both center announcement and right feed. In combat this can repeatedly compete with targets and mission messages.
findings.evidence: Actual core recovery shows duplicate center/feed notification; source confirms kill and supply follow same path. Frequency was not measured in this experience run.
findings.recommendation: Use feed/hitmarker for routine kills and supply. Reserve center announcements for mission phase, core and extraction events.

findings.problem: Spatial objective labels are10px and enemy labels9px, despite larger functional HUD elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Computed/source label sizes and actual spawn/near-core screenshots.
findings.recommendation: Use11–12px objective/enemy labels with restrained backgrounds; retain distance contrast.

findings.problem: New named people disappear into a generic victory panel with only eliminations/time/score. The mission premise now has content but no recovered-person manifest.
findings.evidence: Actual result screenshot shows THE SIGNAL LIVES and generic text; no recovered names or memory recap.
findings.recommendation: List the three recovered people/roles and archive text or access to it on completion.

findings.problem: The level remains a repeated slab courtyard with highly simplified hovering drones and weapon/character presentation. A bright rectangular floor reflection still draws the eye. No authored character performance, cinematic extraction, bespoke soundscape or wider campaign has been demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Continue bespoke environmental storytelling, material/animation/audio work and independent human playtesting. Correctness checks cannot establish AAA quality.

limitations: This is automated browser inspection, not an independent human playtest.
Recon difficulty was selected to inspect experience; this review does not assess Standard balance.
Debug arrangements were used for near-core and final-phase presentation after the normal route met cover.
No source files edited; browser is closed and root may safely change runtime.
A7/10 usability judgment is not a10/10 game or a guarantee of enjoyment.
